items.title: Hentoff Nat — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: The interviewer mentions Hank Jones in a list of musicians ('Hank Jones and Benny Goodman', 'Hank Jones – and you’re there') and asks about the interviewee's relationship with the group. The interviewee responds by discussing his general feeling of not being 'totally part of the tribe' and recounts

ctx.x: Or Clark or Joe Wilder or Hank Jones and Benny Goodman.

Again, speculatively, I think – the three you named, I think if race was a factor, I don’t think it was the major factor. Because after all, Lester Young was The Pres. He was the president of the tenor saxophone. He was treated that way. He didn’t lack for gigs. Norman Granz, for example, would use him whenever he could. Ben Webster, the same way. Ben I think later regretted leaving Ellington for economic reasons, but when he went off to Denmark, he was lionized there, toward the end of his life. In fact…
